research_question: How are LLM-based multi-agent systems evaluated, and which benchmarks, metrics and methods are used?

checks.question: Does the paper study a multi-agent system, with two or more interacting agents? (A single agent, or a standalone LLM, is "no".)
checks.yes: The paper studies a multi-agent system of two or more interacting agents.
checks.no: The paper studies a single agent or a standalone LLM, not a system of interacting agents.

checks.question: Are the agents built on large language models? (Classic agent systems and multi-agent reinforcement learning without LLMs are "no".)
checks.yes: The agents are built on large language models.
checks.no: The agents are not built on large language models, as in classic agent systems or multi-agent reinforcement learning without LLMs.

checks.question: Is evaluating such systems the main contribution? "Yes" means a benchmark, dataset, evaluation framework, metric, an empirical study that compares systems, or a failure analysis; any kind of evaluation counts (performance, safety, reliability, cost). A paper that proposes a new system and also releases a new benchmark or dataset that others can reuse is "yes". A paper that proposes a new system or method and evaluates it only to show that it works is "no".
checks.yes: The main contribution is evaluating such systems: a benchmark, dataset, evaluation framework, metric, empirical comparison of systems or failure analysis, on any aspect such as performance, safety, reliability or cost; a paper that proposes a system and also releases a reusable new benchmark or dataset counts.
checks.no: The main contribution is a new system or method that is evaluated only to show that it works, without releasing a reusable new benchmark or dataset.

checks.question: Is it a primary study, not a survey, review or position paper?
checks.yes: The paper is a primary study.
checks.no: The paper is a survey, review or position paper.
